newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar trims gains but still stays firm.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar trims gains but still stays firm.

text.p: White sugar futures pared some of their earlier gains on Monday afternoon but activity was more subdued in the light of a lacklustre performance in New York, traders said.
With commission house buying strengthening spot October during the early part of the session, selling from trade players was noted later on which took the edge off the gains.
Traders said they thought the buying had been for a fund, although earlier one said a trade client could have been involved.
"The market has been very quiet apart from that," said one, adding that the mundane action in the raws had not inspired any real burst of sentiment in London.
"The spreads have hardly been touched...the premiums were slightly out of line when New York opened but there's not a great deal of business being done.'
At 1605 GMT October was up $1.20 at $324.50 after touching a high of $325.50. December was up $1.50 at $320.70 and overall volume amounted to 1,395 lots.
Market sources said the perception of supply shortages into 1998 was prompting more interest in buying March rather than December.
Results are still awaited in Bangladesh's tender to buy 25,000 tonnes of white crystal sugar for shipment by September 9. Bidding took place on July 20.
The most competitive offer was believed to be at $339.70 a tonne, followed by $343.00.
Paris white sugar futures also gained ground in a light total volume of 127 lots. October and Decem,ber were both up $2.00, at $324.00 and $320.00 respectively.
On the lesser-quality 100 ICUMSA market December was $1.50 higher at $298.00. Volume totalled 40 lots.
